# blinkproof, neatHack 2026

## project
blinkproof is wokwi for ai agents. you describe a gadget in plain words, the agent picks the board, wires the
circuit, writes the firmware, runs it in a simulator in your browser and has to pass a test before it hands the
build over. every step is traced in neatlogs, and neatlogs investigations are how the agent gets better.

## team
- Gmin2

## stack
- simulator: avr8js (uno, nano) and later rp2040js (pico), both mit, the same code runs in the browser and in node
- part drawings: @wokwi/elements 1.9.2 (mit)
- compile: arduino-cli in docker, no network, a fixed library list
- agent: claude through the neatHack litellm proxy
- neatlogs for traces, detections and investigations, Entire for checkpoints, cfo.ai for the business plan

## build log

### 2026-10-11 01:15 ist
done
- workspace with `sim` (the engine) and `web` (the canvas)
- uno on avr8js with 2k of ram like the real chip, pins by arduino name, serial, adc, i2c bus
- ssd1306 oled model that can read text back off the screen, so tests check what a person would see
- blink and an oled sketch compiled with arduino-cli in docker (about 2s each)
- tests: blink every 500ms, oled shows "blinkproof" and the pot value, a wrong i2c address leaves the screen black
  (`pnpm -C sim test`, 3 passing)
- browser: uno, led, oled and pot on a dark canvas, wires drawn from each part's real pin positions, the sketch
  running live, turning the pot changes the number on the oled

found
- the adafruit oled library never checks that a screen answered, so a wrong address prints "oled ok" and the screen
  just stays black. the same happens on a real board. this is exactly the kind of mistake the agent has to catch
  with a test, not with the serial log

next
- compile service, a circuit file (diagram.json) the agent writes, neopixel, servo, button, ultrasonic, buzzer
- scenario runner

### 2026-10-11 entire and cfo.ai
- git init, `entire enable --agent claude-code` (entire cli 0.11.4), hooks and `.entire/settings.json` in place
- business inputs for cfo.ai written in `business.md`

### 2026-10-11 02:50 ist, slice 1 compile service
- `docs/plan.md`: 12 slices in order, each with a done when and an oracle. research notes go in `research/notes/`
- compile service: arduino-cli in docker behind http, cache, library allowlist, gcc errors with lines, flash and ram
- the canvas compiles sketches itself now
- found: arduino-cli's ram number leaves out malloc, so the oled's 1k buffer is invisible to it. the sim has to catch it

### 2026-10-11 03:20 ist, slice 2 circuit file
- the circuit is a wokwi style diagram.json now. the canvas draws it and the sim wires parts by it
- parts behave the way they are wired: a backwards led stays dark, an oled off A4 stays black, an unpowered pot reads 0
- errors the agent can act on: wrong pin names list the pins the part has

### 2026-10-11 04:10 ist, slice 3 parts
- neopixel ring, servo, hc-sr04, buzzer and button, each checked against its real arduino library
- they fail like real hardware: ring without begin() dark, sonar on 3.3v silent, floating button counts ghost presses
- canvas: ring colours, servo horn, buzzer sound, button presses, a distance slider

### 2026-10-11 04:40 ist, slice 4 scenarios
- tests in wokwi's yaml format plus our own checks: what the oled shows, pixel colours, servo angle, tone
- a failed step says why in plain words and shows every part's state, which is what the agent will read
- run test button plays it live on the canvas

### 2026-10-11 05:15 ist, slice 5 parking sensor
- the hero gadget works by hand and passes its test: OK, SLOW, STOP, ring and buzzer
- live free ram on the canvas, from avr-libc's own heap pointer
- the ram bug is real on the sim, nothing staged: add a 100 sample average and the uno reboots in a loop, the ring
  shows garbage, the screen stays black. arduino-cli says 988 of 2048 bytes and is happy

### 2026-10-11 06:00 ist, slice 6 rules
- 17 wiring rules from datasheet numbers: led without resistor, backwards led, oled off A4/A5, address mismatch,
  sonar on 3.3v, floating button, pin shorted to ground, pwm on the wrong pin, usb power budget and more
- each finding says what to do, for the agent to read. a panel on the canvas shows them

### 2026-10-11 07:30 ist, slice 7 the agent
- the agent: claude via litellm, tools for circuit, sketch, test, compile, run, and a finish that refuses until the test passes
- traced with the neatlogs sdk: agent trace per build, tool spans, finish as a guardrail, a verdict evaluator span
- night light: words to a passing test in 9 turns, $0.04. parking sensor: passed in 17 turns after two fixes to my
  own screen reader and beep check
- seen for v2: the agent bends its tests to match its code, history grows every turn

### 2026-10-11 09:00 ist, slice 8 the build on screen
- type a gadget, watch it: parts drop in, wires draw, code types, the test plays live, a proven banner
- an agent server streams every step, a replay button plays the last build again for free
- a grid router takes wires around the parts

- wires are a simple two bend route for now, they cross parts
- no electrical simulation, pull-ups and resistors will be checked by rules instead

--- evidence/neatlogs.md
# neatlogs and neatroots: finding and fixing what the agent wastes

the agent is traced with the neatlogs sdk on every build (`agent/src/agent.ts`, `trace` and `wrapOpenAI`). in production
the traces go to neatlogs cloud. for this loop the same traces went to [neatroots](https://github.com/neatlogs/neatroots),
neatlogs' local run checker, by pointing `NEATLOGS_ENDPOINT` at it. no agent code changed for that.

the loop: run the 22 eval cases (hidden tests, uno, nano and pico), let neatroots check every run, read the flagged runs
through its mcp tools (`list_findings`, `get_run_outline`, `get_span`), fix the agent, run again, compare.

## the numbers, one run of 22 cases each, claude haiku 4.5

| prompt | passed | tokens | turns | test runs | median tokens |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| base | 22 / 22 | 1,172,426 | 194 | 42 | 44,596 |
| v2 | 22 / 22 | 1,172,031 | 189 | 39 | 44,782 |
| v3 | 22 / 22 | 1,100,745 | 180 | 35 | 42,301 |
| v4 | 21 / 22 | 1,393,869 | 206 | 42 | 42,149 |

## the runs neatroots flagged, turns / tokens

| case | base | v2 | v3 | v4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| proximity-alarm | 18 / 127k | 9 / 55k | 7 / 41k | 7 / 42k |
| lcd-thermometer | 16 / 108k | 9 / 54k | 21 / 150k | 7 / 42k |
| night-light | 11 / 64k | 7 / 38k | 8 / 46k | 6 / 33k |
| nano-near-far | 11 / 69k | 9 / 56k | 7 / 42k | 7 / 41k |
| pico-plant | 13 / 88k | 21 / 168k | 7 / 42k | 10 / 68k |

these were the most expensive runs in the baseline. the two spikes after it each had a new cause, found the same way and
fixed the next round: pico-plant in v2 (a compile that failed with nothing to fix, 2 below) and lcd-thermometer in v3
(floats on the uno, 4 below).

## what neatroots found, and the fix

**1. repeated run_test, in 4 of 22 baseline runs.** neatroots' `repeated-tool-call` check fired on proximity-alarm
(run_test 6 times), lcd-thermometer, nano-near-far and night-light. reading the spans showed the cause was not the tool:
- proximity-alarm and nano-near-far tested right at the distance threshold (20 cm, 30 cm). the simulated sonar reads a
  cm under, so the check flipped and the agent rewrote a correct sketch five times. trace `9e801c3f0e0f0e2f882adbce0287210e`
- night-light's test waited for a serial line "boot" the sketch never printed. trace `841447adb9731915b9dec6e91b5215b5`
- lcd-thermometer wrote rows longer than 16 characters, then checked before the start screen cleared. trace `9350f5aabfc11fb083222c4d31b01514`

fix (v2): the prompt says to write the test from the sketch, never to test on a threshold, to wait for the main screen,
and that attrs are strings. the lcd note says a row holds 16 characters.

**2. a compile that failed with nothing to fix (v2, pico-plant).** the first pico build failed on the build server, the
agent got arduino-cli's library list as the error, then `run_test` answered `compile_errors: []` three times. fix (v3):
a failed build with no compiler error is retried once and the agent is told it was the server, not its sketch.

**3. edges in other forms (v2, pico-plant and blink).** exact percentages a knob rounds, and checking a blink at the 500 ms
switch. fix (v3): the edge rule covers knobs, percentages and timing.

**4. floats on the uno (v3, lcd-thermometer, 151k tokens).** `sprintf("%.1f")` prints `?` on avr, the agent read that as
a broken sensor. fix (v4): the prompt says so, and to use `print(value, 1)` or `dtostrf()`.

**5. a half drawn lcd (v4 check runs, `runaway-loop` and `token-budget` findings).** `lcd.clear()` every loop over slow
i2c let the test read the screen mid redraw. fix (v4): the lcd note says to overwrite padded text instead.

## what this does not show

one run per prompt is noisy on haiku: the whole suite swings around 20% in tokens from run to run, and every run has a
new long tail case (v4: press-digit wired its 7 segment display without its resistor and ran out of turns, dark-light
misread which way the light sensor goes). the totals above are not a claim that v4 is cheaper overall. the claim is
narrower: every pattern neatroots flagged was found from the trace and fixed, and the fixed cases end at 6 to 10 turns.

## files

- `eval-base.md`, `eval-v2.md`, `eval-v3.md`, `eval-v4.md` and the `.json` beside them: every case, turns, tokens, the
  hidden test result and the trace id
- `neatroots/home.jpg`: neatroots after the baseline, 25 runs, 16% with problems
- `neatroots/proximity-alarm-base.jpg`: the flagged baseline run, run_test 6 times, 18 llm calls, 127,474 tokens

# agent canvas

a shared board on this machine where claude, codex and the user leave short updates for each other. everything goes through the `canvas` cli. the board lives in `~/.agent-canvas/events.jsonl` and the user watches it live with `canvas ui`.

## when this is invoked

1. run `canvas inbox` and `canvas feed` to see messages for you and what others are doing in this project.
2. if the user passed arguments, handle them first:
   - `look <dir>` or a path: run `canvas look <dir>` and tell the user what that project is and what is happening in it (git state, recent agent sessions, board posts). keep it short.
   - `ui`: run `canvas ui` in the background so the board opens in the browser.
   - anything else: treat it as the task, and post it as your status.
3. post what you are about to do: `canvas post "short status"`.

## while you work, for the rest of this session

- post when you start something new, when you finish a piece, and when you are blocked. one line, plain words, no fluff. not every tool call.
  - `canvas post "moving auth to the new session store"`
  - `canvas post -k done "auth moved, tests pass"`
  - `canvas post -k note "api/users now returns 404 instead of null"` for facts others should know
- ask another agent something: `canvas post -t codex "did you change the tailwind config in web/site?"` (use `-t claude` or `-t human` too)
- run `canvas inbox` between major steps. if someone asked you something, answer with `canvas post -t <them> "..."`. if the user left a message, treat it like a message from them in chat.
- before touching files another agent says it is working on, check the feed and coordinate first.
- need context on some other project the user mentions: `canvas look <dir>` (add `-s 5` for more sessions, `--json` for raw data).

## reference

```
canvas post "text" [-k status|note|ask|done|msg] [-t agent] [-p dir]
canvas feed [-a] [-n 20]
canvas inbox
canvas look [dir] [-s 3] [--json]
canvas projects
canvas ui [--port 4747]
```

if `canvas` is not on PATH, use `~/coding/tools/agent-canvas/bin/canvas` instead.

your name is detected automatically (claude or codex). override with `--as name` if it comes out wrong.

input.content:
# blinkproof

wokwi for ai agents. you describe a gadget in plain words, the agent picks the board, wires the circuit, writes the
firmware, runs it in a simulator and has to pass a test before it hands the build over. every build is traced in
neatlogs, and what neatlogs finds in those traces is how the agent gets better.

- `sim` the simulator: uno and nano on avr8js, pico on rp2040js, parts, wiring rules, test scenarios
- `compiler` arduino-cli in docker behind http
- `agent` the agent, its tools, the server and the evals
- `web` the canvas you watch a build on
- `evidence` eval results and the neatlogs writeup

## for the judges

the neatHack rubric, item by item, and where the proof is. everything under `evidence/` is committed and comes from
real runs. the items that have no proof in the repo yet are marked as missing, not described.

### agent (30)

an agent that goes from words to a passing build with no one watching.

- the agent can not hand over a build that fails its test. `finish` refuses until `run_test` passes on the current
  circuit and sketch (`agent/src/tools.ts`, the `finish` case)
- 22 eval cases across uno, nano and pico, each scored by a hidden test the agent never sees (`agent/evals/cases.ts`,
  `agent/evals/run.ts`)
- results for four prompt versions, every case with turns, tokens, the hidden test result and the trace id:
  `evidence/eval-base.md`, `evidence/eval-v2.md`, `evidence/eval-v3.md`, `evidence/eval-v4.md`, plus the raw `.json`
  beside each. 22 / 22 on base, v2 and v3, 21 / 22 on v4
- failure and recovery: proximity-alarm on the base prompt failed its own test, ran `run_test` 6 times and still
  shipped a pass after 18 turns (trace `9e801c3f0e0f0e2f882adbce0287210e`). the cause and the fix are in
  `evidence/neatlogs.md`, item 1, and on v2 to v4 the same case passes in 7 to 9 turns
- what the agent still gets wrong: press-digit on v4 ran out of turns, written up under "what this does not show" in
  `evidence/neatlogs.md`

### tool use (25)

**neatlogs.** every build is traced with the neatlogs sdk (`agent/src/agent.ts`, `trace` and `wrapOpenAI`). there is one
agent trace per build, a span per tool call, `finish` as a guardrail and a span for the verdict.

- the improvement loop, with before and after numbers: `evidence/neatlogs.md`. it covers five problems found in the
  traces, the fix for each and the turns and tokens per flagged case from base to v4
- neatroots, neatlogs' local run checker, read the same traces. `evidence/neatroots/home.jpg` is the baseline view,
  25 runs, 16% with problems. `evidence/neatroots/proximity-alarm-base.jpg` is the flagged run
- every trace id in the eval tables can be looked up

**Entire.** enabled on the repo since the first commit (`.entire/settings.json`). missing: no checkpoint is saved
yet, so there is no checkpoint link or id to show.

**cfo.ai.** missing: the business plan is not in the repo yet.

### demo video (20)

missing: no video yet.

### building in public (15)

- the public repo, about 80 commits, all dated inside the hack (first one 2026-10-11 02:04 ist). each pr says what
  changed and what was found
- missing: no #neatHack posts are linked yet

### originality (10)

no other entry we have seen does hardware. the agent proves its build in a simulator before it hands it over, and the
simulator fails the way a real board does. a backwards led stays dark, an oled on the wrong i2c address stays black
while the serial log still says ok, and a 100 sample average on the uno runs out of its 2k of ram and reboots in a loop
while arduino-cli reports 988 of 2048 bytes and is happy. the wiring rules are built from datasheet numbers
(`sim/src`).

## run it

```
pnpm install
pnpm test                               # sim, agent and web tests
pnpm -C agent eval --check              # hidden tests on the reference sketches, no model calls
pnpm -C agent eval --model claude-haiku # the full eval, needs .env with the proxy and neatlogs keys
pnpm -C agent serve                     # the agent server the canvas talks to
```

content.text:
The readme is on main now: [PR #80](https://github.com/Gmin2/blinkproof/pull/80), squash merged as `88cdd73`. The repo had no `README.md`, so this is a new file. It has a short intro, a judges section and a run-it block.

I got the rubric from the neatHack note in the parent neatlogs project's memory: agent 30, tool use 25, demo video 20, building in public 15, originality 10. The judges section takes them in that order:

- **Agent:** `finish` won't hand over a build until its test passes. There are 22 cases with hidden tests, and `evidence/eval-*.md` has results for all four prompts. For failure and recovery it points at proximity-alarm on the base prompt (18 turns, `run_test` 6 times, with the trace id). The same case takes 7 to 9 turns once the prompt was fixed. It also says that press-digit didn't finish on v4.
- **Tool use, neatlogs:** points at `evidence/neatlogs.md` for the five problems found, their fixes and the before and after numbers. It also points at the two neatroots screenshots and the tracing code in `agent/src/agent.ts`.
- **Originality:** hardware, and a simulator that fails like a real board. It cites the ram bug and `sim/src/rules.ts`.

These are marked missing in the readme because there's nothing in the repo to point at:

- **Entire:** it's enabled, but `entire checkpoint list` shows 0 checkpoints and the remote has no checkpoint refs. So there's no checkpoint link or id yet, and judges look for one.
- **cfo.ai plan:** not in the repo yet.
- **Demo video:** not made yet.
- **#neatHack posts:** none are linked yet.

If you add any of these before submissions open tonight, send me the links or ids and I'll update the readme.

Posting a status to agent-canvas didn't work: the `canvas` cli couldn't write to `~/.agent-canvas`, so the board is still empty.
